modifier.description:
Value type modifier

Non empty constraint is specified by adding an exclamation mark in front of the ValueType:
```type
  where: !Location
```

The desire to preserve empty values (such that they can be differentiated from the lack of any value) is specified
by adding a question mark in front of the ValueType:
```type
  approved: ?boolean
```

The non optional function parameter constraint is specified by adding `!?` in front of the ValueType:
```type
  f: function(url: !?string serialized Url)
```

@see #isNonEmpty
@see #preservesEmpty
@see #isNonOptionalParam
@see FunctionParam#isNonOptional

keyType.description:
The value type for the keys that index the collection.
For array and set, the key is `int` and for stream is the key is not used.
For maps, the key can be any primitive type.

elementType.description: The value type for the elements of the collection.

title:
"Collection type" is the base type for all specific collection value types: array, set, map and stream.

Collections all share the behavior of holding elements of a single value type.

- An {@link ArrayType array} is a collection whose elements are ordered and are accessed by index.
  Arrays allow nulls or duplicates.
- A {@link SetType set} is a special array which does not allow nulls and duplicates.
  Like arrays, sets are also ordered and accessed by index.
- A {@link MapType map} is an associative array of elements.  The key can be any primitive value type,
  although most maps are indexed by strings.
- A {@link StreamType stream} is a read-once collection.  Streams may be arbitrarily large, larger than can fit into
  memory at any one time, so care should be taken not to materialize them all at once.

For programming convenience, instances of collections use underlying language binding facilities where appropriate:
- In Java, arrays (and sets) implement the java.util.List interface and map collections implement Map.
- In JavaScript, arrays and sets extend Array and maps are objects.
- In Python, arrays and sets are lists and maps are dictionaries.

It is also possible to declare _any collection_ using the `collection<..>` syntax. This refers to any collection
type and specifies only the element type. Instances of any of the concrete collection types are allowed (as long as
the element type is compatible).

@see ArrayType
@see SetType
@see MapType
@see StreamType
